qa_pairs.question: What is multifactor authentication (MFA) and what types of second factors can be used to access services?
qa_pairs.answer: Multifactor authentication (MFA) allows you to protect your account with more than a password. Once your account is configured, you will need to enter your username and password, and then perform a second action (the "second factor") to access most services. You can choose any of these factors for this second authentication step: approving a notification on a smart device through the Duo Mobile application, entering a code generated on demand, or pushing a button on a hardware key (YubiKey).

qa_pairs.question: Why is it strongly recommended to configure multiple options for your second factor when enabling multifactor authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: When you enable multifactor authentication for your account, it is strongly recommended that you configure at least two options for your second factor. This ensures that if you lose one factor, you can still use your other one to access your account. For example, you can use a phone and single-use codes; a phone and a hardware key; or two hardware keys.

qa_pairs.question: How do you register a smartphone or tablet for multifactor authentication using the Duo Mobile application?
qa_pairs.answer: To register a smartphone or tablet for multifactor authentication, first install the Duo Mobile authentication application from the Apple Store or Google Play (ensure you get the correct app, as TOTP applications like Aegis, Google Authenticator, and Microsoft Authenticator are not compatible). Then, go to the CCDB, log in to your account, and select "My account → Multifactor authentication management." Under "Register a device," click "Duo Mobile," enter a name for your device, and click "Continue" to display a QR code. Finally, in the Duo Mobile application, tap "Set up account" or the "+" sign, tap "Use a QR code," and scan the QR code shown to you in CCDB, ensuring your mobile device is connected to the internet.
